Clinical history (case record; may contain prior observations):
age: 43
gender: female
history: We present a 43-year-old woman that presents with franc dyspnea, non-productive cough and central chest pain with 2 weeks of evolution, with no fever, that she associates with a single inhalative high-concentration exposure to bleach, during normal work. She had no pre-existing atopy or pulmonary problems. Two weeks earlier, she went to the emergency department of a private hospital, having been diagnosed with right community-acquired pneumonia, having been medicated with antibiotics and bronchodilator therapy. She returned to the emergency department a week later with aggravated symptoms, due to lack of response to the prescribed antibiotic and bronchodilators. 
Laboratory tests revealed mildly elevated C-reactive protein (12 mg/dL with normal range being <3.0mg/dL) and leukocytosis (17.8x10^9 with 88% of neutrophils) and the oxygen saturation levels were 92%. On auscultation of her chest, widespread expiratory wheeze was noted.

A 43-year-old woman presents with dyspnea, non-productive cough, and central chest pain after exposure to high-concentration bleach. A thorax X-ray is performed (Figure 1), revealing areas of discrete hypotransparency. Based on the X-ray findings and the clinical history provided, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A) Community-acquired pneumonia
B) Chemical pneumonitis with subsequent reactive airways dysfunction syndrome (RADS)
C) Acute eosinophilic pneumonia
D) Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
E) Organizing pneumonia
F) Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
